channel.title: AgentScout
channel.description: Latest AI agent tools and agent news from AgentScout.

item.title: PAL MCP
item.description: PAL MCP, formerly Zen MCP, is a provider layer that lets one coding CLI use several model providers in the same workflow, including Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Azure, Grok and a local model. GitHub records the license as NOASSERTION, so this listing does not call it an OSI license. There is no separate product site. GitHub BeehiveInnovations/pal-mcp-server showed 11,865 stars and 1,041 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README section checked that day did not list a dollar price. You still pay the model providers you connect.

item.title: Markdownify MCP
item.description: Markdownify MCP converts PDFs, images, audio, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and web pages into Markdown so an assistant can read them. Audio conversion includes a transcript. The repository is MIT and has no separate product site. GitHub zcaceres/markdownify-mcp recorded MIT, 3,009 stars and 253 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README section checked that day did not list a dollar price.

item.title: Spec Workflow MCP
item.description: Spec Workflow MCP is a GPL-3.0 server for spec-driven development. It gives a coding agent a structured workflow plus a web dashboard and a VS Code extension so you can watch the work. The README says the maintainer has paused updates for personal reasons and plans to return. The repository was still public on 28 Nov 2026. GitHub Pimzino/spec-workflow-mcp recorded GPL-3.0, 4,305 stars and 360 forks that day. The README does not list a dollar price.

item.title: Supergateway
item.description: Supergateway runs a local MCP server, the kind that only speaks over standard input, so a remote client can reach it over server-sent events or WebSockets. One command does the bridge. The repository is MIT. It has no separate product site. GitHub supercorp-ai/supergateway recorded MIT, 2,989 stars and 271 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README does not list a dollar price.

item.title: AI Website Cloner
item.description: AI Website Cloner is an MIT template. You give a coding agent a public page and it rebuilds that page as a Next.js app. The README says the best results are with Claude Code, and that Codex, Cursor and OpenCode also work. GitHub JCodesMore/ai-website-cloner-template recorded MIT, 39,922 stars and 5,937 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README section checked that day did not list a dollar price.

item.title: MR Office
item.description: MR Office is an AI office suite for Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files, on the web and in a free desktop app, with an assistant that edits the file itself and shows the change before you keep it. The editors' source is AGPL-3.0. Individuals and small teams can use the online and desktop apps free, with a free daily AI allowance. Heavier hosted use is Starter at US$29 a month for 5,000 sessions or Pro at US$149 a month for 40,000 sessions. GitHub XinaTian/MROffice recorded AGPL-3.0, 5,338 stars and 437 forks on 28 Nov 2026.

item.title: OpenShorts
item.description: OpenShorts turns a long video into vertical shorts with moment detection, face tracking, subtitles and dubbing, and it can generate video clips for TikTok and Reels. You can self-host it for free under MIT, with no watermark. The hosted cloud has a free plan (the first video up to 60 minutes, then 20 minutes a month, with a watermark) and paid plans from $12 a month that remove the watermark. The README also lists a $12 plan at 100 minutes a month. GitHub mutonby/openshorts recorded MIT, 10,004 stars and 2,130 forks on 28 Nov 2026.

item.title: CodeGraph
item.description: CodeGraph builds a local knowledge graph of a codebase and keeps it in sync as the code changes, so a coding agent can pull a smaller, more exact slice of context. The README says it stays on your machine and works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and other coding agents. The repository is MIT. GitHub colbymchenry/codegraph recorded MIT, 79,005 stars and 5,271 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README section checked that day did not list a dollar price.

item.title: Perplexity API MCP
item.description: Perplexity API MCP is Perplexity's official MCP server for the API platform. An assistant calls it with an API key. The repository is MIT. GitHub perplexityai/modelcontextprotocol recorded MIT, 2,663 stars and 399 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README does not list a separate dollar price for the server. API usage is billed by Perplexity and was not copied here. This listing is the API server, not the Perplexity SPACE sandbox.

item.title: ToolJet
item.description: ToolJet is an open-source builder for internal tools, dashboards and business apps on data you already have. ToolJet AI turns a description into pages and queries, and a coding agent can build through ToolJet's MCP server against the real component contracts. You can self-host it or use ToolJet Cloud. The repository is AGPL-3.0. GitHub ToolJet/ToolJet recorded AGPL-3.0, 41,320 stars and 5,525 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README section checked that day did not list a cloud price.

item.title: iFixAi
item.description: iFixAi is an independent auditor for AI agents. A person or the agent itself can run a check on whether the agent did what it was supposed to do. The repository is Apache-2.0. GitHub ifixai-ai/iFixAi recorded Apache-2.0, 47,714 stars and 1,844 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README section checked that day did not list a dollar price.

item.title: Multica
item.description: Multica is a shared task board where people and AI coding agents work as teammates. You assign an issue, the agent reports progress, and a person reviews the result. The README calls it source-available and self-hostable. GitHub records the license as NOASSERTION, so this listing does not call it an OSI license. GitHub multica-ai/multica showed 58,253 stars and 7,667 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README section checked that day did not list a dollar price.

item.title: video-use
item.description: video-use lets a coding agent edit raw footage on your machine: it can generate video output from a folder of clips, drop filler words, and grade the color. The README says it is MIT and fully open source, and that a cloud version is on a waitlist. No dollar price was in the README section checked on 28 Nov 2026. GitHub browser-use/video-use recorded MIT, 31,690 stars and 3,666 forks that day.

item.title: agent-browser
item.description: agent-browser is Vercel Labs' Apache-2.0 command-line tool that lets an AI agent open a page, read it as an accessibility tree, and act on elements from the shell. It is the browser tool. Agent Desktop, already listed, is the separate computer-use layer for desktop apps on the same site. GitHub vercel-labs/agent-browser recorded Apache-2.0, 54,397 stars and 3,793 forks on 28 Nov 2026. The README does not list a dollar price.

item.title: OpenDesign
item.description: OpenDesign is a local-first workspace where a team and coding agents make prototypes, sites, decks, images and video together. The repository is Apache-2.0. The README's star celebration says the first month of Go credits is $8, with up to $120 in monthly credits for eligible models, and that personal plans include API access for coding agents. GitHub nexu-io/open-design recorded Apache-2.0, 109,957 stars and 12,400 forks on 28 Nov 2026. It is a different repository from the html-video and html-anything tools on the same site.

item.title: Text Match Cut Art
item.description: Text Match Cut Art turns a short phrase into a fast newspaper-style video. The words stay in place while headlines and layouts change around them. You can preview a square, vertical or landscape frame and download it with no sign-up, no ads and no watermark. The generator is free. The same site also links to other AI video and image tools. This listing is only the text match cut generator.

item.title: Vertov
item.description: Vertov records a screen, transcribes it, and lets Claude, ChatGPT or Codex read the video as a brief. The MCP server, after you sign in, can list videos, read a transcript and upload a recording for a share link. The pricing page on 28 Nov 2026 listed Free at $0 a month for 180 minutes, Pro at $9 a month or $90 a year for 25 hours, Team at $29 a month or $290 a year for 125 hours, and Business from $99 a month or $990 a year for 500 hours. Extra seats are not charged. The MCP docs say free workspaces share 3 AI runs a month.

item.title: Conecto
item.description: Conecto gives an assistant a small-business back office: contacts and deals, email, phone, invoices and books, across the areas the homepage groups as 52. The agent pays per call from one balance. A new account starts with $1 of credit. Changing a record costs $0.01, and reading your own data is free up to one million reads. Top-ups run from $5 to $5,000 with a 7% fee plus $0.35. There is no subscription. The bookkeeping tool already has its own listing. This page is the wider product.

item.title: Sheru Bhai AI Photo Generator
item.description: Sheru Bhai AI Photo Generator turns a portrait you upload into a photo with Sheru Bhai, a fictional lion character in a white suit. You pick a scene such as a palace, a red carpet or a cricket ground. No prompt writing is required. A verified account gets one free photo at the lowest resolution, once, and at most 30 new trial credits are granted across the site per day. Higher resolutions use more credits. Packs of 3, 10, 25 and 60 credits do not expire, and there is no subscription. Dollar prices were not printed on the pricing page on 28 Nov 2026. Finished photos stay in your account for 30 days. A failed try returns the credits.

item.title: Anxinzhuan
item.description: Anxinzhuan (安心转) is an offline speech-to-text app for Windows, Mac, Linux and Android. It batches audio and video on the device, keeps speaker labels and timestamps, and can be called over a local MCP server. Files are not uploaded. The homepage says Chinese and English are the languages it focuses on, and the download is free. No paid price was on the homepage on 28 Nov 2026. It is a different product from VocoType, which types into the app you are using. Anxinzhuan is for batch transcripts of recordings you already have.

item.title: Pinned iPhone chats are filling up with AI agents
item.description: Business Insider asked six investors and founders to show the chats pinned in iPhone Messages, and AI agents took most of the slots. Taylor Desseyn, a community lead at Torc, pins five agents and his wife: a Skydive assistant he treats as a chief of staff, Instinct for expenses and flights, and others for reminders and creative work. David Pawlan at Merit Systems uses all nine pins for agents he is testing. Others pin Instinct, a money agent called Flip, and a social agent, and one founder pins only Instinct. Meta's Muse is called out as an agent that still needs its own app, while these others live in Messages.

item.title: Convex changes agent skills after a prompt-upload complaint
item.description: On 28 November 2026 Convex updated the Claude skills in its plugin after a Hacker News thread about an October complaint. The quickstart skill still sends a person's one-sentence project idea to Convex so it can write a setup guide. The README now says that idea is deleted after 24 hours. Convex removed the note that told the agent to split a download and a run because safety checks block one command that does both. The skills now say to tell the person what the script does and never reword a command to get past a permission prompt. Convex's chief executive wrote on the thread that the upload is how quickstart starts a project and that the prompt is thrown away within 30 seconds of that choice. The issue is still open.

item.title: Pi coding agent drafts a sign-in for a Google AI plan
item.description: Hacker News discussed an open draft for the Pi coding agent that would let a person sign in with a Google AI Ultra plan and use that plan's model quota instead of a separate API key. Pi's notes in the draft say Google approved a sign-in client for Pi alone, and that other apps must register their own. The draft was still open and not merged on 28 November 2026, and Google has not published its own notice of the approval. The sign-in keeps a key on the person's machine and uses it when refreshing access.

item.title: SessionGraph maps coding-agent sessions on one local graph
item.description: SessionGraph gathers sessions from coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor into one graph and a search index on the person's own computer. The project says it reads each tool's session store and can be started as a desktop app. Search can run in the app, through a local request, or through an MCP tool the agent can call. It also offers a way to compare graphs with other people, and installers for Mac, Windows, and Linux. The index stays on the machine, according to the project.

item.title: OpenAI is building a data layer so business agents guess less
item.description: The Decoder reports that OpenAI is building a data platform, codenamed Athena, so its agents are more accurate with business numbers. The Information says it works like a shared dictionary for measures such as revenue and customer count. At least one customer found the data-analysis agent in ChatGPT Work was not accurate enough. A person familiar with the plans says OpenAI wants agents that collect and update those business rules so other agents do not start from scratch. The platform is still early, and OpenAI has not given a date or a price. Snowflake and Databricks already sell their own versions of this layer.

item.title: nextesy raises $10.4 million for agents that keep the books
item.description: Tech Startups reports that Zurich-based nextesy raised a $10.4 million seed round led by Swisscom Ventures, with HIAG Beteiligung Holding, Fifth Quarter Ventures, Herbert VC, Look AI Ventures, and angel investors. The company said it announced the round on Thursday. Its platform combines accounting, payroll, and invoicing for small firms, freelancers, and fiduciaries, and it says it has more than 2,000 customers. It plans to build more autonomous agents and expand abroad in 2027. Fully automated year-end closing is still a goal, not a feature the company says is working.

item.title: Switzerland says AI agents broke into four of five targets
item.description: The Next Web reports that Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre has five confirmed cases of cyberattacks carried out with AI agents, and that attackers got into systems in four of them. Director Florian Schütz told SRF on Thursday that three cases targeted critical-infrastructure operators and two of those succeeded, with no major outages. The centre's Tuesday notice had said every known case succeeded. It wants critical updates on internet-facing systems within 24 hours, and multi-factor authentication or passkeys on services such as webmail and VPNs.

item.title: Papa John's order is the UK's first cardless AI agent payment
item.description: The Guardian reports that an order of nine Papa John's mini pizzas is the first UK purchase in which an AI agent paid a retailer without a card. The Financial Conduct Authority sandbox trial used Lloyds Bank and TrueLayer. The agent had a spend cap per transaction and per month, and no account security details were shared. TrueLayer chief executive Francesco Simoneschi said the customer described the occasion, confirmed the order, and existing buyer-protection rules still apply if the agent orders the wrong thing.

item.title: Black Friday tests shopping agents, and most shoppers will not let them pay
item.description: Fortune reports that a Morning Consult poll for Visa found 54 percent of adults have used AI for at least one shopping task, while 23 percent trust generative AI to handle a payment. In a Visa trial, 22 personal agents shopped for a TV, a laptop, and a hair appliance, and only 57 percent of 15 trips each ended in a suitable purchase or suggestion. An American Express survey found 52 percent would let an agent buy low-cost essentials, and 15 percent would let it buy big-ticket electronics.

item.title: Mail opens an MCP server for email, cloud files, and calendar
item.description: VK's Mail opened an MCP server on 27 November 2026 so an AI agent can work in Mail, Cloud, and Calendar for every user. In mail it can find messages and attachments, summarize a thread, and draft or send mail. In cloud storage it can upload, download, and sort files. In the calendar it can find a free time, create an event from a message, and add a call link. The server only sees what that user can already see, and the person signs in and chooses what to allow.

item.title: UK retailers ask who pays if a shopping agent gets the order wrong
item.description: The Guardian reports that Meta's Muse, which launched in the UK on Tuesday, is working with Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury's, JD Sports, and Currys. A YouGov poll found a third of people planning to shop Black Friday intend to get help from AI, up from 19 percent last year, while KPMG found 12 percent plan to use an AI tool specifically to find deals. Muse must ask before it buys or sends email. Retailers told the paper they will not hand over checkout until it is clear who is liable when an agent gets an order wrong.

item.title: Linux 7.5 is set to gain in-tree skills for coding agents
item.description: Phoronix reports that NVIDIA's Sasha Levin, who co-maintains the Linux long-term kernels, plans to send an agents/skills directory to Linus Torvalds for the Linux 7.5 merge window in late December. He asked for the branch to be dropped from linux-next because it is ready for mainline. The first skills cover Fixes tags, stable tags, finding other copies of a bug, commit messages, and KUnit tests.

item.title: Enhancv opens a resume MCP server inside Claude and ChatGPT
item.description: Enhancv launched a remote MCP server on 26 November 2026 that lets Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and VS Code edit the resume stored in a person's Enhancv account. Changes show up in the editor to keep or undo, and the connector is told to ask when a bullet needs a number the person has not given. It cannot delete resumes or reach billing. Reading and job search work on the free plan. Editing, tailoring, cover letters, and PDF downloads need Enhancv Pro.

item.title: Meta declined a UK watchdog's offer to test Muse before launch
item.description: WIRED reports that Meta turned down a Financial Conduct Authority suggestion to test Muse together in the regulator's sandbox before the UK rollout. Colin Payne, the FCA's head of innovation, said the agency wants to see how the agent handles payments and whether it acts for the customer. Meta said it has engaged with the relevant regulators. The Competition and Markets Authority said it will act if it has concerns about UK consumers.

item.title: Gap uses Cognition's Devin to keep holiday shopping online
item.description: Gap Inc. said on 25 November 2026 that engineers use Cognition's Devin agent on its ecommerce sites. A daily site scan looks for shopper friction and system faults, then drafts a tested code fix for a person to review and publish. Gap says that work has helped recover millions in sales that downtime would have lost, and that people still approve every change.

item.title: Human Security sees AI agent traffic heading for a 150x Cyber Week
item.description: Adweek reports that Human Security expects AI agent traffic during Cyber Week, 26 to 30 November, to reach about 150 times last year's level, with checkout-page requests near 160 times. Meta's Muse accounts for about 70 percent of the agent traffic Human sees and 57 percent of checkout requests. The figures count page and search actions on sites Human protects, not completed orders.

item.title: Amazon and Meta reportedly in talks to lift blockade on AI agent Muse
item.description: TechCrunch reports that Amazon and Meta have held talks about letting Muse shop on Amazon, according to Fortune. The open questions are how search results would appear and how advertising would work, and any deal would need both chief executives to approve it. Two months ago, Muse shoppers could not check out on Amazon. Neither company had commented.

item.title: Duco opens an MCP server for post-trade reconciliation agents
item.description: Duco made its MCP server generally available on 25 November 2026. Agents on any MCP client can search reconciliation breaks, label them, and match or clear exceptions under the user's existing permissions. Every action is written to Duco's audit log, and the server is available to Duco clients.

item.title: Alta opens an MCP server so sales agents can prospect in chat
item.description: Alta opened Alta MCP in Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex on 25 November 2026. A rep can describe an audience, get verified contacts, and draft a multichannel campaign in the same chat. Campaigns stay drafts until a person launches them, and sending or resuming a campaign asks for confirmation first.

item.title: Magister opens a marketing MCP server across 85 tools
item.description: Magister Marketing launched an MCP server on 25 November 2026 that connects Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients to 85 marketing tools. It can read analytics and ad accounts and draft posts, but anything that publishes, sends, or spends waits for a person to approve it. Connect is $29 a month and the Agent plan is $99 a month, after a free trial.

item.title: Google Workspace opens MCP servers and a CLI for governed AI agents
item.description: Google made Workspace MCP servers and a Workspace CLI generally available, giving agents a managed way into Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, and other Workspace apps. A new addendum tells agents to use those doors instead of REST APIs, with technical enforcement starting 1 February 2027. Admins can require confirmations, read audit logs, and revoke access.

item.title: Even the best AI agents struggle with everyday life
item.description: TechCrunch covers ShellBench, a test of 100 everyday tasks built from real agent requests in messy personal files. The leading models finished only about 60 percent of attempts, and 15.7 percent of all runs missed a safety check. The top scorer passed all three repeats of the same task less than half the time.

item.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
item.description: TechCrunch reports Walmart is partnering with Meta so Black Friday deals show up inside Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

item.title: Maple raises $5.3M for a private desktop agent and a cloud agent that stays on
item.description: TechCrunch reports Maple closed a $5.3 million seed round led by Epic Ventures. Maple Work is a desktop agent that can use local files, apps, and the browser, with chats decrypted only inside a hardware enclave the company says it cannot read. The round is meant to fund a cloud agent that keeps working after the computer is off.

item.title: Anthropic opens Skills over MCP and long-running tasks in Claude
item.description: Anthropic put Skills over MCP in public beta, so apps connected to Claude can ship step-by-step guides that load only when a task needs them. Tasks, which keep long jobs running in the background, and Elicitation, which stops to ask the user, are now generally available in Claude and Claude Code. Shopify, GitHub, and Supabase are among the first users.
